title: Quick check: Query Parameters

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Query Parameters”?
options: The concept removes the need to consider error states or accessibility.
The browser will infer all application behavior even if inputs and state are contradictory.
The concept allows application code to mutate React-managed DOM and state directly.
Search parameters should preserve URL semantics, history behavior, and an intentional fallback state.
questions.answer_key: Search parameters should preserve URL semantics, history behavior, and an intentional fallback state.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Query Parameters: Search parameters should preserve URL semantics, history behavior, and an intentional fallback state.

questions.prompt: Which practice is most reliable when applying Search parameters?
options: Store duplicate copies of every value so each component can change it independently.
Optimize by adding every available Hook without measuring the result.
Use route links and test direct deep links, browser history, and unmatched paths.
Skip validation because a successful render proves that the application is correct.
questions.answer_key: Use route links and test direct deep links, browser history, and unmatched paths.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Query Parameters: Use route links and test direct deep links, browser history, and unmatched paths.

questions.prompt: What should you verify before considering “Query Parameters” complete?
options: Rely only on a screenshot of the happy path and never repeat the test.
Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
Check only whether the file exists; syntax and runtime behavior do not matter.
Assume a client-side check proves that a remote service accepted the change.
questions.answer_key: Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Query Parameters: Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
